precepts.text: Every sweet smelling tree shall overshadow Israel, for God shall lead Israel with joy; overshadow means to lead.
precepts.point: Thy cousin Elisabeth hath also conceived a son in her old age, for with God nothing shall be impossible; also means the same way, and the impossible thing is a barren old woman bearing, not a birth without a father.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Baruch gives another one. Overshadow does not mean that it got her impregnated. It means to guide her to where she had to go. “For God hath appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God”.

“Moreover even the woods and every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God. For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory”. The trees shall overshadow Israel, for God shall lead Israel. To overshadow is to lead, guide or defend.

So in Luke 1:35 the Lord would lead Mary to Joseph. When it says overshadow thee, it means he will guide and lead her, like he led Zacharias home to his wife to lay with her. That is what it is talking about, not him overshadowing her into pregnancy.

precepts.text: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold thy children gathered from the west unto the east by the word of the Holy One. By this word is what is going to gather the children of Israel back together. He is telling Peter: it is time; awake; rise; now it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel.
precepts.point: Rise, Peter: it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. Kill: kill the old man, mortify yourself, discipline yourself. Eat: devour wisdom, learn the scripture. And then go out and teach. But in that time there was no New Testament: Peter would have to explain it to those of the circumcision using the Old Testament.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
We know now the vision is referring to man. So what is the “Rise” talking about? What was the whole purpose of the vision? To gather the northern and southern kingdoms back together, to gather us back from where we were scattered, east to west, north and south.

Baruch uses the same word: “Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold thy children gathered from the west unto the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God.” The children are coming from the west unto the east, and they rejoice when they remember God.

They are gathered “by the word of the Holy One.” That word is what is going to gather the children of Israel back together. This is it right here.

So when the voice says “Rise, Peter”, he is telling Peter: it is time. Awake. Rise. Now it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. The arising comes first; then comes the kill and the eat, because before we gather the twelve tribes we first have to be made ready to teach them.

precepts.text: God will lead Israel with joy; the mercy and righteousness that come from Him are His glory.
precepts.point: Israel is God's glory, so declaring His glory among the heathen means the so-called blacks, native Indians, and Hispanics are coming back to their glory, coming back to God's law, statutes, and commandments. God is putting us back in order among the heathen; we are coming back to our traditions and our heritage and leaving the heritage of the heathen.

note.label: Psalm 96: Declare His Glory Among the Heathen

precepts.why:
What is God's glory? “For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that cometh from him.” His glory goes into many things: the mercy and righteousness that come from him are his glory, and Israel walks in the light of it.

God leads Israel with joy back into that light. That is what declaring his glory among the heathen looks like: the so-called blacks, native Indians and Hispanics coming back to God's law, statutes and commandments, back to our traditions and heritage, leaving the heritage of the heathen behind.
